decisions.reason: The NL requirement 'the system can transition to DoorShutWithItem if the door is closed with zero time set' uses an 'if' clause that in state-machine semantics denotes a guard condition. The working contract's transition group NL-GROUP-NL4-DOOROPENWITHITEM explicitly separates event='door closed' from guard='zero time set' as independent normative parts. The closed model transition:line:22 has guard=null and the model declares zero variables, making any guard expression inexpressible. The structural absence of the required guard on an otherwise correctly bound transition (source=DoorOpenWithItem, target=DoorShutWithItem, event=Door_Closed) establishes the violation. The alternative composite-event reading (treating 'door is closed with zero time set' as a single indivisible event description) is defeated by the supplied transition-group structure that explicitly decomposes the requirement into separate event and guard components. response.basis: Supplied numbered NL segments NL1-NL8, primary typed plan with 21 contracts and 5 transition groups, and the stage-context-projection.v8 manifest identifying the natural-language author source and closed FCSTM model.
response.reason: I performed a segment-by-segment completeness check of the primary typed plan against all eight numbered NL segments. Every initial-entry obligation (NL1), every source-target endpoint (NL1-NL8), every independently required effect (NL6 cancel/update cooking time; NL8 stop timer), every state action (NL5 display/update cooking time in ReadytoCook; NL7 start timer in Cooking), and every multi-alternative shared-source transition group (NL1 DoorShut, NL4 DoorOpenWithItem, NL5 DoorShutWithItem, NL6 ReadytoCook, NL8 Cooking) is already represented. The NL does not establish: explicit cardinality or member-set obligations; separate containment declarations beyond what is implicit in the flat state-machine structure; event-consumer coverage scoped beyond individual source states; guard-disjointness requirements (the alternatives are distinguished by different events, not by overlapping guards that must be mutually exclusive); progress or deadlock-freedom obligations; or termination semantics. Single-source single-target sentences in NL2, NL3, and NL7 are fully captured by their endpoint contracts with source and target binding hints; adding single-alternative groups would not introduce an independently violable obligation beyond what the endpoint contracts already assert.
